input:
∫ (log(cot x)) / sin 2x dx =

Options:
A. -log(cot x)² + c, where c is constant of integration.
B. 2(log(cot x))² + c, where c is constant of integration.
C. (-1/4)(log(sin x))² + c, where c is constant of integration.
D. (-1/4)(log(cot x))² + c, where c is constant of integration.

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate the indefinite integral ∫ (log(cot x)) / sin 2x dx.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Substitute t = log(cot x). Then dt = (1/cot x)(-cosec²x) dx = (-sin x / (sin²x cos x)) dx = -2 / (2 sin x cos x) dx = -2 / sin 2x dx. Thus dx / sin 2x = -dt / 2.

key_concepts: Integration by substitution: t = log(cot x)
Derivative of log(cot x): dt = -2 / sin 2x dx
Power rule for integration: ∫ t dt = t²/2 + c

key_formulas.dt_derivation: d/dx[log(cot x)] = (1/cot x)(-cosec²x) = -1/(sin x cos x) = -2/sin 2x

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Substitute t = log(cot x), express dx/sin 2x in terms of dt, evaluate ∫ t (-dt/2), and replace t with log(cot x).
logical_steps: Step 2: Differentiate: dt = (1/cot x) · (-cosec²x) dx = -1/(sin x cos x) dx = -2/(sin 2x) dx
Step 4: Rewrite integral: I = ∫ t · (-dt/2) = -1/2 ∫ t dt
Step 5: Integrate: -1/2 · (t²/2) + c = -1/4 t² + c = -1/4 (log(cot x))² + c

step_2_differentiate.dt: 1/cot x · (-cosec²x) dx = (sin x / cos x) · (-1 / sin²x) dx = -1 / (sin x cos x) dx
step_2_differentiate.sin_2x_identity: sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x  ⇒  sin x cos x = (sin 2x)/2

phase_5_verify_answer.answer: D. (-1/4)(log(cot x))² + c, where c is constant of integration.
